title: H4984 (124th General Assembly): Access to Firearms by Children

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2022-02-16; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess124_2021-2022/prever/4984_20220216.htm (LegiScan doc 2518914))
provenance.note: Introduced text (Feb. 16, 2022). The Kingston Act. Third- and first-degree offences (misdemeanour up to one year; felony up to thirty years), definitions and the gifting clause (16-23-650) not quoted.

operative_text:
Section 2 (new Section 16-23-630): (A) It is unlawful for a person to leave an unsecured firearm in a place where a child could access the firearm. The fact that a child is able to access an unsecured firearm constitutes prima facie evidence that the unsecured firearm was left in a place where a child could access it.
Section 2 (new Section 16-23-630(C)(1)-(2)): A person commits the offense of unsecured firearm in the second degree if the person leaves an unsecured firearm in a place where a child could access the firearm, and a child discharges the firearm causing bodily injury to the child or another person. A person who violates the provisions of this subsection is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction, must be imprisoned not more than twenty years.
Section 2 (new Section 16-23-640): (A) It is unlawful for a person to authorize a child to use a firearm except when the child is under the direct supervision of a responsible adult.
Section 2 (new Section 16-23-620(8)): 'Child' means a person seventeen years of age or less.
